title: Window C, pass 2 (M8, session 3 task S3T-8; RESUME section 7 step 9): confirmation window on devoff4b (S4b + S4c, every switch OFF by default). s0 (all OFF) vs win3 = the three winners together (p2fc + d11p + q500) vs c1np = fix (i) + C1 v3 without P2 (verify off) vs p2fc (W6's winner, the anchor). Round 1 is the GPU warm-up and is discarded in the read-out
notes: Pass 2 of 2. Pass 1 is matrix-windowC.json: the same arms with the same switches in file order s0, win3, c1np, p2fc; this file reverses it (p2fc, c1np, win3, s0), so round 1 starts with another arm and the arm that follows each arm is reversed. Pool both passes in the read-out.

GO (night launcher, bench/agent5/launch): 'GO WC2 matrix-windowC2.json <sha256> only=s0,win3,c1np,p2fc repeats=4' (-Only keeps this file's order p2fc, c1np, win3, s0): the launcher adds -ColdShared, so 1 unscored cold run (devoff4b) + 4 round-robin rounds x 4 arms = 17 runs, runner estimate about 39 min. Without the anchor: 'only=s0,win3,c1np repeats=4' (same file and sha256), 13 runs, about 30 min.

GPU warm-up (RESUME section 7 step 0; W6.md L222-226): the runner has no discarded-run option, and the launcher's -Repeats sets every arm's repeats, so the warm-up is round 1: the cold run plus round 1 give ~11 min (4 arms) or ~9 min (3 arms) of game load before round 2, against the 5-13 min the GPU needs to reach its steady 832 MHz. The read-out drops round 1 (all arms, tags *-r1) and scores rounds 2-4; check gpu.csv that round 2 starts at the steady clock, and drop more if not. Rounds 2-4 rotate the start arm (shifts 1, 2, 3 of the file order), so the scored rounds are 3 rows of a 4x4 Latin square (3 arms: a full 3x3 square).

Question: (1) do the three winners hold together on one bin (win3 vs s0)? W6 (p2fc), W9 (q500) and W5b (d11p) timed them only one at a time, W5b on devoff4 (S4a). Expect fps about +18 % and about -1 core or more (p2fc -0.25, q500 -0.75, d11p -0.20 core) if they add up. (2) C1 without P2 (c1np vs s0; c1np vs p2fc = P2's share with C1 on). (3) p2fc vs s0 repeats W6 as the anchor that ties this window to W6.

Arms (all on build/agent2/devoff4b-bin, MANIFEST sha256 DE11A914079D7DF7, legodimensions.exe DFBE1D43B28861A6; S4a's #38 timer_queue.cpp is in it: its MANIFEST says 'PASS rexruntime.dll contains timer_queue_precise_wait', and every cvar below is a string in rexruntime.dll / rexgpu-xenos.dll, the two env keys in legodimensions.exe). s0: every switch OFF (W6's s0, W9's off). win3: p2fc's 4 cvars + the 8 timer cvars (the bundle of W5b's d11) + timer_queue_precise_wait=true (d11p) + LEGO_GPU_WAIT_BACKOFF_US=500 and LEGO_GPU_WAIT_SPIN_US=30 (W9's q500). c1np: physical_protect_hold_global_lock=true + physical_protect_keep_watch=true + physical_protect_keep_watch_verify=false (W6's fc). p2fc: W6's p2fc. Switches at launch only (C1 and #38 are kInitOnly).

Proof per run, before any number is read: win3 and p2fc and c1np game.logs each have 'C1 keep-watch: on (with physical_protect_hold_global_lock)' and 'C1 keep-watch: first kept protect at', and no 'C1 verify: on'. win3 also has 'Host timer resolution set to 1 ms (background opt-out on)', exactly one 'TimerQueue: precise wait (timer_queue_precise_wait)' and exactly one 'GPU wait back-off: ON (quantum 500 us, spin 30 us); stats OFF; GetData hook built.', and run.json env_set holds LEGO_GPU_WAIT_BACKOFF_US=500 and LEGO_GPU_WAIT_SPIN_US=30; TimerQueue < 15 % of a core in threads.csv. s0, c1np and p2fc have no back-off line, no precise-wait line and no LEGO_GPU_WAIT_* key. s0 has no C1 line. No arm may log 'Recovered stale physical page protection', 'Unhandled guest physical write fault', 'PhysicalHeap::Protect failed' or 'is not a plain number'. P2's ON proof is the cvar list in run.json.

Gates before the GO (Overseer's call): a functional (untimed) PASS of win3's full set on devoff4b (all three together were never run), and of c1np's set (C1 without P2 is unverified, not failed: RESUME section 6 item 2; timing it is not a verdict on its safety). Any STUCK-LOCK follows the finding-10 rule (RESUME section 6 item 3).

Read-out: per pair the difference of medians with a 95 % CI over the scored rounds of both passes (6 per arm), median ms, fps, p99, the 1 % low, process cores and the render / GPU Commands / TimerQueue thread ms/f. A timing claim needs a CI that excludes 0. Window hygiene (W5b.md section 7): flag runs with non-game load >= 2.8 cores and give the verdicts with and without them.

Window: 5 s settle + 55 s warm-up from the first frame, then 50 s measured (every window >= 60 s after the first frame; the runner flags window_before_floor below 59.5 s); the cold run 55 s warm-up, 30 s window. One frame source: perf.csv (frames perf), uncapped (framerate_limit=0); one driver (drivers/thread-cpu.ps1). Runner flags on every run: --audio_mute=true --pause_when_unfocused=false --native_settings_load=false --discord_rpc=false. sys_csv on.

Timing comes only from the user's unlocked desktop through the night launcher; agent runs of this matrix (-Quick, hidden desktop) are functional only. Compare within this window only (host state of 2026-11-25).

arms.note: p2fc = W6's winner (P2 + fix (i) + C1 v3, verify off), the anchor. Proof: the two C1 lines, no 'C1 verify: on'
c1np = fix (i) + C1 v3 without P2, verify off (W6's fc). Proof: the two C1 lines, no 'C1 verify: on'
win3 = p2fc (P2 + fix (i) + C1 v3, verify off) + d11p (8 timer cvars + timer_queue_precise_wait) + q500 (back-off 500 us, spin 30 us). Proof: the C1, 1 ms, precise-wait and back-off lines (notes)
s0 = devoff4b with every switch OFF (W6's s0, W9's off)
